additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder (BED) is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food within a discrete time period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control over eating, and followed by marked distress. Unlike bulimia nervosa, individuals with BED do not regularly engage in inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as purging, fasting, or excessive exercise, and weight status can range from normal to obese. Episodes often occur in response to emotional stress, negative mood, or interpersonal difficulties, and the disorder is frequently associated with shame, secrecy, and impaired quality of life. The course can be chronic or fluctuating, with many patients presenting only after weight gain, medical concerns, or functional and emotional consequences become difficult to manage.

patient.stressor: About fourteen months ago, Fumi increased her night-shift hours as a commercial cleaner after dropping to part-time status in community college, telling herself she would use the flexible schedule to build a design portfolio but instead finding her days and nights increasingly unstructured. Long stretches alone in office buildings, irregular meal breaks, and easy access to vending machines and leftover catered food gradually turned late-night snacking into a habitual way to stay awake and unwind after stressful shifts and creative blocks. As her art projects stalled and she felt further from her dream of becoming a designer, she became more reliant on solitary eating at odd hours to cope with frustration and the guilt of procrastinated coursework and paperwork. She finally sought psychiatric care when her eating patterns began to feel out of control, she noticed significant weight gain affecting her comfort playing basketball and running with the club, and a supervisor’s comment about "raiding the breakroom" left her embarrassed enough to bring it up at a campus counseling center referral.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like once I start eating after my night shifts, I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating.
